current_end_date_iso.reason: WLBT (Aug. 11, 2026) reports the moratorium 'is expected to go into effect on Thursday' (Aug. 13, 2026), the 30th day after the non-unanimous July 14 passage, consistent with the packet's own 30-day-effective-date analysis. 183 days from 2026-08-13 is 2027-02-12.

current_status.from: Adopted July 14, 2026 by a 5-2 council vote; no further council vote is required for it to take effect. Because the vote was not unanimous, the ordinance does not take legal effect until 30 days after passage (approximately August 13, 2026), then runs 183 days from that effective date. As of the July 31, 2026 research date the ordinance had passed council but had not yet reached its effective date. During the moratorium the city will not accept, process, or approve data center applications for special or conditional use permits, zoning map amendments, building permits, or other zoning changes. Approximately 1,100 acres of city-owned land around Jackson-Medgar Wiley Evers International Airport are exempted.
current_status.to: Active as of 2026-09-23. The moratorium took legal effect on or about August 13, 2026 (30 days after the July 14 passage) and runs 183 days from that date, through approximately 2027-02-12. On August 11, 2026 the Council separately passed a non-binding resolution (introduced by Ward 3 Councilman Kenneth Stokes) urging the administration to identify appropriate data-center sites; it does not alter or shorten the moratorium, which remains in force. During the moratorium the city does not accept, process, or approve data center applications for special or conditional use permits, zoning map amendments, building permits, or other zoning changes; about 1,100 acres of city-owned land near Jackson-Medgar Wiley Evers International Airport remain exempted. No repeal, extension, or replacement ordinance was found in sources reviewed through 2026-09-23.
current_status.reason: Confirms the moratorium actually reached its effective date and remains active, and records the August 11 non-binding resolution so it is not mistaken for a status change.

outcome.from: Enacted by council vote; scheduled to take legal effect approximately 30 days after passage.
outcome.to: Enacted by council vote 5-2 on July 14, 2026; took legal effect approximately August 13, 2026 and runs 183 days from that date (to approximately February 12, 2027). A separate non-binding August 11, 2026 council resolution urging site identification does not change the moratorium's status.
outcome.reason: Updates the outcome narrative now that the effective date has passed and the moratorium is confirmed in force.

evidence.title: Jackson passes state's first data center moratorium
evidence.supports: Confirms the 5-2 vote adopting the citywide data center moratorium on July 14, 2026, the airport-land exemption amendment, and that the council can extend or cancel the moratorium at any time.
evidence.quote: The Jackson City Council voted Tuesday to approve a citywide data center moratorium. It is the first city in Mississippi to do so. ... 'This council has voted to go in the right direction,' Grizzell said after the moratorium passed 5-2

evidence.title: See details on the latest council resolution regarding data centers in Jackson

evidence.quote: The council approved the six-month moratorium on July 14. The measure was amended from the floor to exempt city-owned property near the Jackson-Medgar Wiley Evers International Airport. The ban is expected to go into effect on Thursday.

decisions.notes: No further council action (extension, repeal, or replacement ordinance) affecting the moratorium's term was found through 2026-09-23.
